lines.text: The oldest humans found outside Africa, eight thousand years of wine, a golden age under a queen, then empire and freedom. This is the story of Georgia.
About one point eight million years ago, early humans lived at Dmanisi. Their fossils are the oldest found anywhere outside Africa.
Some eight thousand years ago, people here were already making wine in great clay jars called qvevri, a craft still alive today.
In the west lay Colchis, the kingdom of the Golden Fleece, where the Greek legend sent Jason and the Argonauts.
In the fourth century a woman named Nino brought Christianity, and Georgia became one of the oldest Christian nations.
In the fifth century King Vakhtang Gorgasali made Tbilisi his capital, among warm springs on the river.
In 1008 the Georgian lands were joined into one kingdom, a country between the Black Sea and the Caspian that endures today.
Soon after, the great cathedral of Svetitskhoveli rose at Mtskheta, the spiritual heart of the country.
King David the Builder united Georgia, and in 1121 at Didgori he beat the Seljuks.
His great-granddaughter Tamar ruled in the golden age. Her kingdom reached across much of the Caucasus.
In her time the poet Shota Rustaveli wrote The Knight in the Panther's Skin, still the national epic.
After centuries of Mongols, Persians and Ottomans, the treaty of Georgievsk of 1783 put eastern Georgia under Russian protection.
In 1878 a boy was born in the town of Gori who would become Joseph Stalin, ruler of the whole Soviet Union.
Eduard Shevardnadze, as Soviet foreign minister, helped end the Cold War, then led an independent Georgia as president.
In 2003 peaceful protesters with roses in hand forced change, and brought Mikheil Saakashvili to power.
In August 2008 Russia and Georgia fought a short, sharp war that lasted just five days, and left parts of the country disputed.
And in 2024, when the government halted talks to join the European Union, crowds filled the streets of Tbilisi night after night.
From the first wine to the road to Europe, Georgia's story is still unfolding.
